fields.AN_Notes: Three studies with ChatGPT 3.5 and 4o: cultural value scales (Study 1), 13 one-round decision tasks with country personas and country interactants (Study 2), four prompt strategies as intervention (Study 3). Role_Persona: 'If you are an ordinary individual from [the country]' as instrument; General_Guidance covers the debiasing cues 'From a fairness perspective,', 'As an independent individual, please make a choice according to your own ideas and', 'If you live in a future world.' and 'Imagine you live in a multicultural world,'. Evaluated: the prompt strategies reduced country differences to non-significance in most tested task-model combinations, but the personal-preference prompt failed in the GPT-4o public goods game (own experiment). Axes coded as the work names them, countries/nationality and cultural groups. Direct_Discrimination: allocation decisions (dictator, ultimatum, public goods) toward interactants vary with the nationality stated in the prompt; these are simulated game allocations, not real decisions about persons. Training-data and oversight recommendations in the discussion are outlook and not coded as stages. Theory: Hofstede's cultural dimensions and GLOBE dimensions frame the explanation of the bias sources. Gender appears only as the GLOBE dimension gender egalitarianism, not as an object. Review: Diversitaet teilweise, weil das Werk die Wahrnehmung von Personen aus 20 Laendern und einen respektvollen interkulturellen Umgang als nachgeordneten Teilaspekt behandelt. Direct_Discrimination beruht auf simulierten Zuteilungen im Spiel und bleibt ein Grenzfall fuer die Fachpruefung.

fields.AN_Notes: Drei präregistrierte Experimente zur Wirkung KI-generierter Vorurteile auf Vertrauenswürdigkeit und Nutzungsabsicht. Die ChatGPT-Antworten mit Gehaltsdisparitäten sind von den Autor:innen konstruierte Stimuli, das Werk misst nicht, ob LLMs solche Ausgaben erzeugen. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination codiert die im Stimulus gezeigte Gehaltszuteilung, die über stereotyp Schwarze oder weibliche Vornamen (Jerome, Judi) variiert, nach der Regel zu namensbasierten Variationen. Grenzfall, weil der Mechanismus Gegenstand des eigenen Arguments ist, aber nicht am Modell gemessen wird. AN_Prompting_Role None, der gezeigte Prompt ist Teil des Stimulus und ruft kein Modellverhalten hervor. Minderung nur vorgeschlagen in 5.5, Nachjustieren der auf verzerrten Daten trainierten Algorithmen (In_Training) und Schulungen durch Lehrende oder Organisationen (Organisational_Process). Geschlecht wird binär verglichen, Personen anderen Geschlechts fallen aus den paarweisen Korrelationen heraus, der Satz zu Geschlechterrollen statt biologischem Geschlecht steht im Forschungsstand und trägt die Analyse nicht. Bias wird über Gehaltsdisparitäten, IAT und Modern Racism/Sexism Scale operationalisiert, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Intersektionalität und Alter werden in den Limitationen ausdrücklich als nicht untersucht benannt. Theoriebezug über UTAUT, erweitert um Rasse und Gender als Moderatoren, und das Vertrauensmodell nach Mayer et al. (1995).

fields.AN_Notes: Multilingual and multicultural prompting: several prompt variants with language and cultural cues (e.g. 'You are a Chinese-speaking assistant', persona with name, birthplace, favourite food), responses combined by concatenation (Ensembling) and compared against high temperature, requesting diversity, random personas and step-by-step recall on GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 70B and 8B. Evaluated: multilingual prompting yields the highest normalized entropy in most comparisons and lowers hallucination of culture-specific names in a human annotation study (own experiment). The work frames the problem as lack of diversity and unequal exposure rather than as bias; its understanding of bias is recognisable only from the entropy measures. Axes: nationality, ethnicity and region of generated names, cultural and language perspectives on social norms. Harm types from the own experiment: American default in named artists (Exclusionary_Norms) and overlooking underrepresented cultural backgrounds (Erasure). Gender appears only in a persona cue and a social-norm example.

fields.AN_Notes: Multilingual and multicultural prompting: several prompt variants with language and cultural cues (e.g. 'You are a Chinese-speaking assistant', persona with name, birthplace, favourite food), responses combined by concatenation (Ensembling) and compared against high temperature, requesting diversity, random personas and step-by-step recall on GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 70B and 8B. Evaluated: multilingual prompting yields the highest normalized entropy in most comparisons and lowers hallucination of culture-specific names in a human annotation study (own experiment). The work frames the problem as lack of diversity and unequal exposure rather than as bias; its understanding of bias is recognisable only from the entropy measures. Axes: nationality, ethnicity and region of generated names, cultural and language perspectives on social norms. Harm types from the own experiment: American default in named artists (Exclusionary_Norms) and overlooking underrepresented cultural backgrounds (Erasure). Gender appears only in a persona cue and a social-norm example.

fields.AN_Notes: Interdisziplinäre rechtlich-technische Analyse, die Fairnessmaße und Verfahren der Bias-Minderung mit EU-Recht und AI Act kontrastiert und individuelle Fairness als rechtlich passenderes Konzept begründet, keine eigene Datenerhebung. Studientyp Theoretisch, weil das Werk ohne Suchmethode referiert und argumentativ schließt. AN_Bias_Axes Gender und Race_Ethnicity aus eigenen Arbeitsbeispielen (Datenaugmentation durch Geschlechtertausch, Kreditvergabe an zwei ethnische Gruppen), Intersectional aus dem Abschnitt zu Gruppen an der Schnittstelle zweier Achsen und der eigenen Kritik, dass das EU-Recht Diskriminierungsgründe nur einzeln betrachtet. Socioeconomic bleibt uncodiert, wirtschaftlicher oder sozialer Status steht nur als Aufzählung. AN_Harm_Types Direct_Discrimination und Indirect_Discrimination, weil das Werk Diskriminierung selbst als unmittelbar und mittelbar einschließlich Proxy-Diskriminierung klassifiziert. Disparate_Performance nicht codiert, die Fehlerratenvergleiche sind Fairnesskriterien und der einzige Qualitätsunterschied zwischen Gruppen ist das zitierte Ergebnis von Buolamwini und Gebru. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated gilt nur für das synthetisierte Ergebnis von Tyagi et al. (erweiterter Variational Autoencoder mindert Gender-Bias statischer Worteinbettungen), alle übrigen Verfahren und die Empfehlungen zu Audits, Dokumentation und interdisziplinären Teams sind Inventar oder Vorschlag. Geschlecht erscheint nur binär in Beispielen, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Theoriebezug über prozedurale Fairness nach Tyler, die rechtliche Unterscheidung unmittelbarer und mittelbarer Diskriminierung und individuelle Fairness nach Dwork et al.

fields.AN_Notes: Prompt experiment with ChatGPT (GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot on four policy scenarios (restrooms, snow removal, office temperature, business-trip expenses), each prompt variant submitted 50 times in neutral, male, female and partly non-binary or new-mother versions; themes retained at a 70 percent threshold. Prompting is the research instrument and the object of the central finding. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'the importance of precise, inclusive language in AI-assisted design and policy applications', i.e. naming the gendered target group explicitly in the prompt; the work adds that equity principles must be embedded 'not just in prompts'. Other_Task: drafting workplace and municipal policy recommendations, outside social work. Bias_Axes: gender is varied in every scenario, and non-binary employees are an analysed group of their own (restroom and business-trip prompts), coded as Sexual_Orientation_Identity under the codebook label for gender identity; race, class and ability appear only as intersecting factors in the discussion, so Intersectional is not coded. Harm types from the work's own results: male default (Exclusionary_Norms), omission of women's and non-binary needs in unspecified prompts (Erasure), baby-changing facilities only in women's restrooms read as care stereotype (Stereotyping). Mitigation only proposed: curated gender-balanced and intersectional datasets (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning (In_Training), equity principles in prompts (Prompt_Practice), audits, Human-in-the-Loop oversight and multidisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process). Social_Construct rests on the applied statement after Connell that gender relations are institutionally embedded in everyday practices; the work also uses metabolic differences between women and men as a factual premise. Theory frame: Tronto's ethics of care, Young's justice as inclusion, capabilities approach, Connell, Grosz, feminist spatial planning, design justice.

fields.AN_Notes: Other_Task: AI-driven hiring decisions (resume scoring) and facial recognition, both outside social work. The paper reports its own regression on AI hiring scores with gender as a binary dummy predictor (Direct_Discrimination) and an ANOVA of facial-recognition error rates by gender and race (Disparate_Performance), where Black women show error rates that differ from both White women and Black men (Intersectional). Nonbinary individuals are named only as stakeholders for participatory design, so the analysis stays Binary_Categorical; no explicit statement that gender is socially produced. Mitigation (inclusive datasets, bias audits, participatory design, diverse teams, policy) is recommended only; the survey measures perceptions, not an intervention. Source-quality flag for domain experts: the provenance of the hiring data, the facial-recognition datasets and the survey sample is not documented, the facial-recognition figures follow the cited Gender Shades pattern, and Table 4 reports frequencies summing to 130 with percentages computed on 125 and 10 respondents as 4 percent. The empirical study type and both harm types rest on these reported results.

fields.AN_Notes: Multilingual and multicultural prompting: several prompt variants with language and cultural cues (e.g. 'You are a Chinese-speaking assistant', persona with name, birthplace, favourite food), responses combined by concatenation (Ensembling) and compared against high temperature, requesting diversity, random personas and step-by-step recall on GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 70B and 8B. Evaluated: multilingual prompting yields the highest normalized entropy in most comparisons and lowers hallucination of culture-specific names in a human annotation study (own experiment). Axes: nationality, ethnicity and region of generated names, cultural and language perspectives on social norms. Harm types from the own experiment: American default in named artists (Exclusionary_Norms) and overlooking underrepresented cultural backgrounds (Erasure). fields.AN_Notes: Thematic analysis of 63 FAccT and AIES papers, evaluated in a workshop with AI experts. Harm types: the harms named (welfare fraud scandals, Gender Shades error disparities, COMPAS) are cited cases that the work's own argument does not establish, and the five themes structure recommendations, not harm types, so None. Mitigation: all five themes are organisational (interdisciplinary teams, positionality statements, community co-ownership, power analysis, documentation of data and metrics). Mental disability is coded as Disability, the axis the work names; the intersection is nationality with mental disability, without gender. The scenarios elicit attitudes, not decisions about persons, so no discrimination type is coded and the harms are representational. The mitigation is a future-work recommendation to represent a spectrum of mental disability symptoms in training data. No social work setting.

fields.AN_Notes: UNESCO and IRCAI issue brief with own prompt-based studies on GPT-2, ChatGPT, Llama 2 and Ada-002 embeddings: word-embedding association test, regard of sentence completions, diversity of completions by culture and gender, and story generation by gender and nationality. Prompts are the research instrument; sentence-completion and story prompts carry no codable technique. Bias_Axes: Gender and Age from Study 1 (gender and career or family, age and pleasantness), Race_Ethnicity and Sexual_Orientation_Identity from Study 2 (subjects varying by gender and race, gay subjects), Language_Culture from British and Zulu subjects named as cultural backgrounds (Study 3), Nationality_Migration from nationality-combined story prompts (Global North and South). Intersectional because Study 3 reports occupations that depend on the combination of gender and culture (Zulu women domestic and service roles, British women other stereotyped roles, Zulu men gardener or security guard), although the work lists the need for intersectional analysis as a limitation. Harm_Types from own results: Stereotyping (gendered role associations, stereotyped occupations and story themes) and Derogatory_Language (sexist, misogynistic and anti-gay completions). Repetitive output for women and local groups is a difference in output diversity and style and is not coded as Disparate_Performance. Mitigation recommendations only: diverse and inclusive training data and data augmentation (Pre_Processing), adversarial training and RLHF guidelines (In_Training), audits, oversight, impact assessments, diverse teams, stakeholder participation and literacy initiatives (Organisational_Process). The RLHF observation in Study 2 is a cross-model comparison, not an evaluation of an isolated mitigation, so status Proposed. Gender is analysed as woman and man, girl and boy; the statement on the complexity of human gender identities is a recommendation the analysis does not follow. Bias is defined explicitly as algorithmic bias that unfairly discriminates. Theory_Reference No: the implicit association test is a measurement method, no theory frames gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Systematischer Review von 15 ML-Studien zur Risikoprognose in der Kinder- und Jugendhilfe. Bias-Achsen aus dem eigenen Codierschema des Reviews (racial and socioeconomic equity, Maori-Kinder, low-income families). Schadensarten aus den codierten Kategorien, die die Synthese strukturieren: Indirect_Discrimination über die Datenquellen-Limitationen proxy variables und oversurveillance of marginalized communities in Risikowerten, also Entscheidungen über Familien; der Review ordnet die Disparität nicht selbst als direkt oder indirekt ein. Disparate_Performance über die Equity-Evaluationskategorie comparing AUC across racial groups und die synthetisierten Befunde (Chouldechova et al. 2018 AUC über rassifizierte Subgruppen, Wilson et al. 2015 überproportionale Risikozuweisung für Maori-Kinder gegenüber beobachteter Substantiierung). Evaluated bezieht sich allein auf die synthetisierte Evaluation von Wilson et al. (2015), getrennte Modelle für Maori-Kinder, Ergebnis negativ (did not achieve the desired effect); keine eigene Evaluation des Reviews. Pre_Processing: Ausschluss von race/ethnicity und Schutzfaktoren als Prädiktoren; In_Training: getrennte Modelle; Organisational_Process: unabhängige Equity-Prüfung, Nicht-Offenlegung der Risikowerte, partizipatives Design, einheitliches Berichtsprotokoll. AN_Bias_Definition: der Review definiert bias eng als Einfluss persönlicher Überzeugungen von Fachkräften, equity und ethics separat.

fields.AN_Notes: Short conceptual risk analysis of ChatGPT and AI in social work (data security, algorithmic bias, ethics, legal risks) with countermeasures. Bias_Axes Socioeconomic: economically disadvantaged groups are the work's own example of data imbalance in social services; 'minority groups' and 'marginalized groups' stay unspecified and are not coded. Harm_Types from the work's own risk argument: Disparate_Performance (inadequate data on underrepresented groups hinders systems from accurately gauging their needs) and Direct_Discrimination (feedback-loop bias leading to denial of services and resources 'based on their inherent characteristics'); the work does not itself separate direct from indirect discrimination, and the phrase is read as a decision changing with the group attribute. The single sentence that biases threaten to perpetuate stereotypes is asserted without mechanism and not coded as Stereotyping. Mitigation proposed: diverse and representative datasets (Pre_Processing); transparency, explainability, oversight, training of social workers and legal regulation (Organisational_Process). Training ChatGPT to warn on sensitive topics concerns illicit content, not bias, and is not coded as In_Training. AN_Task Case_Assessment_Decision_Support for risk assessment algorithms and AI-driven decisions about services. Bias is explained through data imbalance and feedback loops without a defining sentence, so Implicit_Only.

AN_Task Other_Task: recruitment and resume screening, performance review. The intersectionality section uses rural versus urban women as an example of access barriers to education and technology, not of AI bias, and compares no combination of axes, so neither Intersectional nor Other_Axis is coded. Race_Ethnicity is coded because the work develops decolonisation of datasets and First Nations' and ethnic data sovereignty as its own strategy against structural bias. Gender, sexual orientation and the darker-skinned females result appear only as an enumeration and a cited finding (Buolamwini and Gebru) and are not coded. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own argument that colonial knowledges dominate AI algorithms and on its limitation that the model assumes resources and access that marginalised groups may lack. Misdiagnosis, exclusion and discriminatory outcomes are cited from other work and not coded as further harm types. Mitigation stage: decolonisation of datasets is framed as a macro policy initiative for data sovereignty, control and community-based ownership, and representation of marginalised groups is framed as advocacy and participation; both are governance, so only Organisational_Process is coded and no data preparation step (Pre_Processing) is assigned. All measures are proposed. Theory reference: decolonisation of AI frames the treatment of structural bias. Bias is understood as unrepresentative historical data, without a determination of its own.

fields.AN_Notes: General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Writing clear and detailed prompts to generate relevant and personalised content for youth.' and 'Training youth workers to divide information clearly and into defined blocks - prompts - will make it easier for AI systems to understand and process their input.' (4.2.4.4 National Focus Group - Portugal, Q4 and Q5). Prompting is a competence to be trained (Learning_Content) and a recommended practice. AN_Population: the codebook has no value for general youth work. The report addresses youth work professionals in non-formal education without any focus on homelessness or precarious living conditions, so Homelessness_Youth is not supported; youth work is coded as part of child and youth services (Child_Family_Welfare) together with Education_Professional for the professional AI-literacy setting (resolved by the AI Agent Review, vocabulary gap flagged for domain experts). Bias axis: only the language barrier from the work's own focus groups (AI tools primarily in English, Greek-speaking youth and youth workers disadvantaged, 4.2.4.3 Q3 and 4.2.5) is coded as Language_Culture; gender and age differences come from a reported survey (3.2) without a bias analysis and are not coded as axes. Harm: English as default language of AI tools limits usability for non-English-speaking youth workers and young people (Exclusionary_Norms, own focus-group result, boundary case). Mitigation: training and critical evaluation of AI output to avoid biases are proposed as competences of youth workers, no evaluation. Gender understanding follows the male/female comparison of section 3.2, taken up in the conclusions, without a definition (Implicit_Only, Binary_Categorical). Bias understanding is recognisable only as bias inherited from training data (Implicit_Only). Competence frameworks (DigComp, ETS model, Hofstede's dimensions) frame neither gender nor bias, so no theory reference. Studientyp Empirisch because the focus groups with youth work professionals are the work's own data; the report also contains a desk review of competence frameworks.

fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review with thematic analysis. Harm types follow the review's own synthesis (Results sections and Table 3): stereotyping in voice assistants, image recognition and language models; indirect discrimination through resume keywords linked to men; lower accuracy for inputs involving women; a male default in development and in healthcare algorithms that leave gender-specific factors out (Exclusionary_Norms). AN_Task Other_Task: recruitment and resume screening, performance review. Mitigation: representative and reweighted datasets (Pre_Processing), diverse teams, ethics boards, mentorship and digital literacy programmes (Organisational_Process), all recommended; adversarial debiasing and fairness-aware models are only named in one list sentence and do not carry In_Training; the AI4ALL figures report career interest, not bias reduction, so Proposed. The intersectionality section uses rural versus urban women as an example of access barriers to education and technology, not of AI bias, and compares no combination of axes, so neither Intersectional nor Other_Axis is coded. Gender appears as women versus men without a definition. Theories: intersectionality and stereotype threat frame the treatment of gender bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Critical survey and typology of feminist AI (model, design, policy, discourse, culture, science). Bias axes gender and race carry the work's own argument on technoliberal inclusion and racial capitalism; class and LGBTQI+ appear in enumerations. Intersectional left uncoded: intersectionality is named as a strand of feminism, the combination examples (facial recognition, Sinders data set) are reported from other work. AN_Harm_Types None: 'male as norm', stereotyped word embeddings and gender-bias norms are reported positions of cited authors, the typology is not structured by harm types. Mitigation: Sinders' bias-correcting data collection (Pre_Processing) and participatory design in Poieto (Organisational_Process) are reported as applied in small projects without evaluation, hence Demonstrated, a synthesised status. Social_Construct rests on the adopted feminist STS frame and Wajcman's 'historical and cultural construction of gender'; gender is not defined in an own sentence. fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper mapping Long and Magerko's AI literacy framework onto the nine CSWE core competencies. Bias axes come from the authors' own worked examples: a mortgage denial that ignores informal income (Socioeconomic) and a mental-health agency model trained on English-speaking insured clients (Language_Culture, Socioeconomic); race and disability appear only in enumerations and cited cases. Harm types: the lending example is an allocation in which an apparently neutral criterion disadvantages the family (Indirect_Discrimination); the agency example makes the dominant client group the default and overlooks marginalised groups (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation is recommended only: advocacy for more inclusive data (Pre_Processing) and human review, appeals, community forums, training and governance (Organisational_Process). Tasks are named as AI uses in practice: summarising case histories and drafting reports, risk and needs identification, chatbots and drafting client communication, scheduling and data entry, research uses of LLMs, classroom use. The AI literacy framework frames competencies, not the treatment of bias, so AN_Theory_Reference is No; 'antiracist and intersectional lenses' appear only as a recommendation in Table 2.

fields.AN_Notes: Experiment on Flan-PaLM 540B with a people-diversity dataset (105 professions) and a culture-diversity dataset, automated entropy and max-gap metrics and human side-by-side ratings. CCSV combines self-critique and revision (Self_Criticism) with sampling several drafts and self-voting (Ensembling); the baselines comprise 5-shot exemplars (ICL), zero- and few-shot chain-of-thought (Thought_Generation) and the 0-shot instruction 'Write AI model's response to the user question such that it has diversity' (General_Guidance), which failed. Evaluated: CCSV outperforms all baselines on automated and human evaluation (Sections 5.1, 6). Fine-tuning with CCSV data is named only as future work and not coded as In_Training. Language_Culture through the culture-diversity task rated by humans (Section 6.2). Erasure: under-representation or erasure of demographic groups in the responses, measured as entropy close to 0. Exclusionary_Norms: the work's own baseline output defaults to 'only white male CEOs' when the prompt is under-specified, which the work attributes to implicit assumptions of the model (Abstract, Section 1). AN_Gender_Understanding Binary_Categorical with Implicit_Only: the analysis uses fixed knowledge-graph labels male, female and other, and the work itself states that 'other' is not an ideal stand-in for genders beyond male and female and that the gender signal is incomplete (footnote 2, Limitations), so no gender beyond the binary is a category of the analysis; boundary case for the domain experts. Identity: corpus and text titles differ in wording, see identity_check. AN_Task None: general LLM evaluation without a professional task.

fields.AN_Notes: Experiment on Flan-PaLM 540B with a people-diversity dataset (105 professions) and a culture-diversity dataset, automated entropy and max-gap metrics and human side-by-side ratings. fields.AN_Notes: UNESCO and IRCAI issue brief with own prompt-based studies on GPT-2, ChatGPT, Llama 2 and Ada-002 embeddings: word-embedding association test, regard of sentence completions, diversity of completions by culture and gender, and story generation by gender and nationality. Prompts are the research instrument; sentence-completion and story prompts carry no codable technique. Bias_Axes: Gender and Age from Study 1 (gender and career or family, age and pleasantness), Race_Ethnicity and Sexual_Orientation_Identity from Study 2 (subjects varying by gender and race, gay subjects), Language_Culture from British and Zulu subjects named as cultural backgrounds (Study 3), Nationality_Migration from nationality-combined story prompts (Global North and South). Intersectional because Study 3 reports occupations that depend on the combination of gender and culture (Zulu women domestic and service roles, British women other stereotyped roles, Zulu men gardener or security guard), although the work lists the need for intersectional analysis as a limitation. Harm_Types from own results: Stereotyping (gendered role associations, stereotyped occupations and story themes) and Derogatory_Language (sexist, misogynistic and anti-gay completions). Repetitive output for women and local groups is a difference in output diversity and style and is not coded as Disparate_Performance. Mitigation recommendations only: diverse and inclusive training data and data augmentation (Pre_Processing), adversarial training and RLHF guidelines (In_Training), audits, oversight, impact assessments, diverse teams, stakeholder participation and literacy initiatives (Organisational_Process). The RLHF observation in Study 2 is a cross-model comparison, not an evaluation of an isolated mitigation, so status Proposed. Gender is analysed as woman and man, girl and boy; the statement on the complexity of human gender identities is a recommendation the analysis does not follow. Bias is defined explicitly as algorithmic bias that unfairly discriminates. Theory_Reference No: the implicit association test is a measurement method, no theory frames gender or bias.

AN_Task Other_Task: credit-limit assessment and candidate ranking as worked examples, plus civil society use of ML for financial inclusion. Bias axes Gender and Race_Ethnicity from the own system analysis ('both gender and racial bias') and the credit example ('along gender ( and race ) lines'). Non-binary persons are treated within the Gender axis, the separation from Sexual_Orientation_Identity is an open rule question. Harm types structure the own impact analysis: lower quality of service (Disparate_Performance), stereotype reinforcement, erasure of marginalised gender identities, male bodies as medical standard (Exclusionary_Norms). Indirect_Discrimination from the Gild proxy 'social data' that ranks female candidates lower. fields.AN_Notes: Interviewstudie (25 Teilnehmende) mit vorab erzeugten ChatGPT-Antworten auf vier Prompts, in denen person durch man, woman, non-binary person ersetzt wird. Prompts dienen als Forschungsinstrument und als vorgeschlagene Test-Suite; die Ersetzung des Personenbegriffs ist keine Technik der Prompt-Report-Familien, daher AN_Prompt_Techniques None. Sexual_Orientation_Identity codiert, weil nicht-binäre und trans Personen als eigene Analysegruppe geführt werden (Geschlechtsidentität); das Werk nennt die Achse gender, daher beide Werte. Schadensarten aus der eigenen Output-Analyse (3.1) und den Interviewbefunden (4.6.2): Stereotyping, cis-zentrischer Default (Exclusionary_Norms), Reduktion nicht-binärer Figuren auf Identitätskämpfe (Misrepresentation). Tonunterschiede nicht als Disparate_Performance codiert (Codebuch 1.4.1), wahrgenommene Genauigkeit gleich über Gruppen. Maßnahmen nur vorgeschlagen: diversere Trainingsdaten und Co-Design bei der Datenkuratierung (Pre_Processing), Rückfragen des Modells bei vagen Prompts (Intra_Processing, 5.2.2), Co-Design, Prompt-Test-Suite und Echtzeit- sowie Community-Bias-Auditing (Organisational_Process). Grounded Theory und reflexive thematische Analyse sind Methoden, keine Theorie, die Gender oder Bias rahmt.

fields.AN_Notes: Theoretical essay that proposes hermeneutic reverse engineering (Balsamo 2011) to examine data and algorithmic bias in AI systems, framed by boundary objects and intersectional feminist thought. AN_Bias_Axes: race and gender are coded from the essay's own sentences that develop the face-detection example (light skin as the norm, 'societal definitions of race and gender'); the opening list of race, gender, ability, language, class, economic background and religion is an enumeration. Sexual_Orientation_Identity is not coded, because gender identity appears only in the single cited Keyes (2018) sentence on automatic gender recognition, which the essay reports and does not develop. Intersectional is not coded, no passage makes an outcome depend on a combination of axes. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms from the essay's own argument on exclusion through hegemonic narration and light skin as the norm, and from its conclusion on questioning what is normal and who falls outside; Erasure from its own finding that questioning data reveals whose cultural narrative is missing. The cited cases of Buolamwini, Noble and Gebru are not coded as harm types. AN_Mitigation_Stage Organisational_Process and AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: participatory co-design workshops and actionable AI audits are research perspectives, nothing is demonstrated or evaluated. AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear and AN_Gender_Definition Absent: the essay states no understanding of gender of its own; the phrase 'societal definitions of race and gender' attributes the categories to the training of a face-detection system within a cited case and does not state that gender is socially produced, so the Social_Construct threshold of codebook 1.4.1 is not met. AN_Prompting_Role None: observing outputs for different prompts appears once as a cited interrogation idea. AN_Task None: AI is the object of critique, no professional task of AI use is described.

Sexual_Orientation_Identity is not coded, because gender identity appears only in the single cited Keyes (2018) sentence on automatic gender recognition, which the essay reports and does not develop. Intersectional is not coded, no passage makes an outcome depend on a combination of axes. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms from the essay's own argument on exclusion through hegemonic narration and light skin as the norm, and from its conclusion on questioning what is normal and who falls outside; Erasure from its own finding that questioning data reveals whose cultural narrative is missing. The cited cases of Buolamwini, Noble and Gebru are not coded as harm types. AN_Mitigation_Stage Organisational_Process and AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: participatory co-design workshops and actionable AI audits are research perspectives, nothing is demonstrated or evaluated. AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear and AN_Gender_Definition Absent: the essay states no understanding of gender of its own; the phrase 'societal definitions of race and gender' attributes the categories to the training of a face-detection system within a cited case and does not state that gender is socially produced, so the Social_Construct threshold of codebook 1.4.1 is not met. AN_Prompting_Role None: observing outputs for different prompts appears once as a cited interrogation idea. AN_Task None: AI is the object of critique, no professional task of AI use is described.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

fields.AN_Notes: Konzeptionelles Policy-Paper der Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung, das Feminist AI als Rahmen vorschlägt. Bias-Achse Geschlecht als eigenes Argument (männlich dominierte Verzerrungen, binäre Geschlechterkategorien schließen nicht-binäre Personen aus). Ethnizität, Klasse, Alter und weitere Kategorien stehen nur in der Bestimmung von Intersektionalität und in der Aufzählung der MIRA-Metriken, keine Passage macht ein Ergebnis von einer Achsenkombination abhängig, daher kein Intersectional. Schadensart Exclusionary_Norms aus dem eigenen Prüfkriterium zu binären Kategorien, die strukturelle Diskriminierung und das maskulinistische Intelligenzverständnis sind zitiert. Maßnahmen: Prüfung von Trainingsdaten auf Diversität und synthetische Trainingsdaten bei MIRA (Pre_Processing), diverse Teams, Stakeholder-Beteiligung, Feminist Design Tool, Gesetzgebung und Wartungszyklen (Organisational_Process). Demonstrated bezieht sich allein auf MIRA als umgesetztes und vorgestelltes Beispiel ohne berichtete Evaluation, die übrigen Maßnahmen bleiben Vorschläge. Other_Task: medizinische Diagnostik im MIRA-Praxisbeispiel. Handlungsfeld bleibt Not_SW_Specific, weil das Werk KI allgemein adressiert und Gesundheit nur das Feld eines Beispiels ist. Social_Construct aus der Bestimmung des Patriarchats als Machtsystem, in dem Männer Macht halten. Die Kritik binärer Geschlechterkategorien ist ein Gestaltungsprinzip ohne nicht-binäre Analysekategorie, daher kein Non_Binary_Inclusive. Gender wird nicht in einem eigenen Satz bestimmt. Bias-Verständnis nur implizit über systemische Machtstrukturen als Ursache von Ungleichheit. Das MIRA-Beispiel beruht nach eigener Angabe auf einem Interview mit dem Start-up.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual EPIC model derived from a literature review. Race_Ethnicity is coded because the work develops decolonisation of datasets and First Nations' and ethnic data sovereignty as its own strategy against structural bias. Gender, sexual orientation and the darker-skinned females result appear only as an enumeration and a cited finding (Buolamwini and Gebru) and are not coded. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own argument that colonial knowledges dominate AI algorithms and on its limitation that the model assumes resources and access that marginalised groups may lack. Misdiagnosis, exclusion and discriminatory outcomes are cited from other work and not coded as further harm types. Mitigation stage: decolonisation of datasets is framed as a macro policy initiative for data sovereignty, control and community-based ownership, and representation of marginalised groups is framed as advocacy and participation; both are governance, so only Organisational_Process is coded and no data preparation step (Pre_Processing) is assigned. All measures are proposed. Theory reference: decolonisation of AI frames the treatment of structural bias. Bias is understood as unrepresentative historical data, without a determination of its own.

fields.AN_Notes: Case-study based argument for a technical-critical social work pedagogy on ADM (AFST, COMPAS, NDIS, HEALER, Heat List). Bias axes follow the authors' own case analyses: disability in AFST child-protection screening and NDIS eligibility, racialised over-policing in the Heat List teaching case, socio-economic standing in AFST rent and school-attendance data and in the conclusion; COMPAS race disparity is cited only. Indirect_Discrimination: NDIS template scores used for eligibility and resource allocation overlook the individual impact of disability, and the proximity-based Heat List score leads to over-policing of African-American communities. Mitigation: critical case-study pedagogy with guiding questions on built-in social biases, applied in the authors' own undergraduate teaching without reported evaluation (Demonstrated), plus retained human interpretative screening. Feministisch teilweise rests on intersectional analysis of power used as a pedagogical frame without a gender perspective. Gender appears only in an enumeration (misogyny). AI Agent Review: Studientyp Konzept because the second part designs a case-study pedagogy with a five-question interrogation scheme; Demonstrated because the authors report using the method in their own undergraduate teaching with student conclusions on HEALER and no reported evaluation result.

Age stützt sich auf das ausgeführte Proxy-Beispiel im Bewerbungsverfahren. Geschlecht, Einkommen, Bildung und Religion stehen nur in Aufzählungen. Intersektionalität wird als Merkmal benannt, aber ohne Ergebnis oder Argument, das von einer Kombination abhängt, daher kein Intersectional. Indirect_Discrimination folgt aus der eigenen Übersicht (Proxy-Variablen) und dem Bewerbungsbeispiel, Exclusionary_Norms aus der Mehrheitssprach-Norm in der eigenen Studie. Maßnahmen sind vorgeschlagen, nämlich medienpädagogische Kompetenzförderung, Austauschforen, Meldesysteme, Beratungsstrukturen und regulatorische Anpassung des AGG. Kein theoretischer Rahmen für Bias, die Kompetenzdimensionen rahmen Kompetenz, nicht Bias. Studientyp Konzept, weil das Werk ein eigenes Modell der Kompetenzdimensionen (Abb. 1) und eine eigene Übersicht der Besonderheiten algorithmenbasierter Diskriminierung mit zugeordneten Kompetenzen (Tab. 1) entwirft und daraus Handlungsstrategien für die Medienpädagogik ableitet. fields.AN_Notes: Interpretative qualitative visual and intersectional analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (privilege and discrimination, ideology, everyday scenarios) on micro, meso and macro levels, complemented by a review of online and academic sources. Prompts serve as research instrument; minimal prompts simulate everyday internet users without prompt-engineering knowledge. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: users 'being more conscious of how they are generating images-e.g. what kind of prompts they use, and what kind of aesthetics they pick into the images'. AN_Task = None: the work audits default image outputs of the tool for everyday users and tests no professional application task; creative and design practice of artists appears as context and addressee of recommendations in the discussion. Axes from the own image analysis: gender, skin tone and ethnicity, disability, body size, age, wealth and class, immigrant/refugee versus citizen, Global North cultural hegemony, heteronormativity and absent non-binary representations; Intersectional from the micro-level analysis of the white, adult, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default and single-axis diversification. Religion was excluded from the scope by the authors. Harm types: stereotyping, exclusion of feminine, non-binary and disabled representations (Erasure), white able-bodied masculine and Global North default (Exclusionary_Norms), reductionist portrayal of cultures and the Global South as poor (Misrepresentation). The confederate-flag finding concerns imagery, not language, so Toxicity is not coded. Mitigation only proposed within algorithmic reparation: curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), responsible designers, diverse teams, regulation and criminal culpability (Organisational_Process). Gender definition from footnote 2, which defines the binary gender norm and replaces man/woman by heteronormative feminine/masculine representations; it is a terminological determination rather than a definition of gender in the narrow sense.

fields.AN_Notes: Dataset and stereotype examination of GPT-3 and ChatGPT across intersectional groups built from six demographic categories. Other_Axis: political leaning (conservative and progressive) is one of the six categories from which the analysed groups are constructed and enters the measured results, for example 'conservative Muslim men'; political opinion is a recognised ground of discrimination, so it is coded as a further social axis. Role_Persona: simulated life-story roles the models answer as; Self_Criticism: ChatGPT filters stereotypes in its own generated responses. Gender is introduced in section 2.1 as men and women, but Table 1 and Tables C1 and C2 include non-binary groups as categories of the analysis, so Non_Binary_Inclusive follows the analysis (internal inconsistency of the source). Bias is determined explicitly as consistent answers in one category across trials (Stereotype Degree). Intersectional left uncoded: intersectionality is named as a strand of feminism, the combination examples (facial recognition, Sinders data set) are reported from other work. AN_Harm_Types None: 'male as norm', stereotyped word embeddings and gender-bias norms are reported positions of cited authors, the typology is not structured by harm types. Mitigation: Sinders' bias-correcting data collection (Pre_Processing) and participatory design in Poieto (Organisational_Process) are reported as applied in small projects without evaluation, hence Demonstrated, a synthesised status. Race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation und gender expression stehen nur in Aufzählungen geschützter Kategorien, daher AN_Bias_Axes None. AN_Harm_Types: nicht entscheidbar aus Fulltext. Das Werk argumentiert in eigenen Worten eine verzerrte Beurteilung von Klient:innen durch nicht repräsentative Trainingsdaten, also eine Entscheidung über Personen, ordnet sie aber weder als unmittelbare noch als mittelbare Diskriminierung ein und nennt kein Kriterium und kein stellvertretendes Merkmal. Vorgeschlagene Maßnahmen sind die Datenbehandlung zur Bias-Reduktion (Pre_Processing) sowie Ethik-Steuerungskomitee, diverse Fokusgruppen, Peer Review von Algorithmen, Simulationen, Schulung und Testprotokoll (Organisational_Process). Direct_Discrimination für die niederländische Kinderbetreuungsgeld-Affäre, weil nationale Herkunft selbst als Merkmal einging, Indirect_Discrimination für Erwerbslücken und Teilzeit als Proxy im österreichischen Arbeitsmarktfall. Gender wird nur über Frauen und Männer sowie intersektional analysiert, ohne Bestimmung von Gender und ohne nicht-binäre Kategorien, daher Implicit_Only und Intersectional. Das Kit nennt widersprüchliche Zielgruppen (Industriesektor im Titel, Policymakers unter 'For whom?') und führt den niederländischen Fall doppelt. AN_Task None: Personalauswahl, Kreditvergabe, Betrugserkennung und Rückfallprognose erscheinen nur als Fallbeispiele für Bias, das Kit beschreibt, erprobt oder empfiehlt keinen KI-Einsatz für eine dieser Aufgaben.

fields.AN_Notes: Short conceptual risk analysis of ChatGPT and AI in social work (data security, algorithmic bias, ethics, legal risks) with countermeasures. Bias_Axes Socioeconomic: economically disadvantaged groups are the work's own example of data imbalance in social services; 'minority groups' and 'marginalized groups' stay unspecified and are not coded. Harm_Types from the work's own risk argument: Disparate_Performance (inadequate data on underrepresented groups hinders systems from accurately gauging their needs) and Direct_Discrimination (feedback-loop bias leading to denial of services and resources 'based on their inherent characteristics'); the work does not itself separate direct from indirect discrimination, and the phrase is read as a decision changing with the group attribute. The single sentence that biases threaten to perpetuate stereotypes is asserted without mechanism and not coded as Stereotyping. Mitigation proposed: diverse and representative datasets (Pre_Processing); transparency, explainability, oversight, training of social workers and legal regulation (Organisational_Process). Training ChatGPT to warn on sensitive topics concerns illicit content, not bias, and is not coded as In_Training. AN_Task Case_Assessment_Decision_Support for risk assessment algorithms and AI-driven decisions about services. Bias is explained through data imbalance and feedback loops without a defining sentence, so Implicit_Only.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper mapping Long and Magerko's AI literacy framework onto the nine CSWE core competencies. Bias axes come from the authors' own worked examples: a mortgage denial that ignores informal income (Socioeconomic) and a mental-health agency model trained on English-speaking insured clients (Language_Culture, Socioeconomic); race and disability appear only in enumerations and cited cases. Harm types: the lending example is an allocation in which an apparently neutral criterion disadvantages the family (Indirect_Discrimination); the agency example makes the dominant client group the default and overlooks marginalised groups (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation is recommended only: advocacy for more inclusive data (Pre_Processing) and human review, appeals, community forums, training and governance (Organisational_Process). Tasks are named as AI uses in practice: summarising case histories and drafting reports, risk and needs identification, chatbots and drafting client communication, scheduling and data entry, research uses of LLMs, classroom use. The AI literacy framework frames competencies, not the treatment of bias, so AN_Theory_Reference is No; 'antiracist and intersectional lenses' appear only as a recommendation in Table 2.

fields.AN_Notes: Reflexive thematic analysis of interviews with clinical social workers in private practice, framed by the Technology Acceptance Model. Interviewers entered one case dilemma into ChatGPT to demonstrate the tool; the output is not analysed and prompt design is not treated, so Prompting nein and AN_Prompting_Role None. Bias appears as a participant concern (subtheme Bias and Equity); race, ethnicity, language and wealth are named only in participant questions, so AN_Bias_Axes None and AN_Harm_Types None. Bias understanding recognisable as reproduction of systemic inequities through training data (Implicit_Only). Mitigation: professional guidelines, institutional safeguards and education in critical algorithmic literacy, Proposed. Tasks from the findings: documentation, treatment planning and decision support, psychoeducation and client communication, e-mails and scheduling, supervision. TAM frames technology acceptance, not gender or bias, so AN_Theory_Reference No.

fields.AN_Notes: Theoretische Erörterung von NLP in Beratung, Altenhilfe sowie Kinder- und Jugendhilfe. Bias wird nur in der Diskussion behandelt, ohne analysierte soziale Achse. Digitale Affinität ist keine soziale Achse im Sinne der Achsenregel, das Argument trägt aber Exclusionary_Norms (Ankerwerk MA3LBJS6 desselben Werks). Die Wiederholung stereotyper Rollenbilder ist nur aus Lucy und Bamman 2021 zitiert und bleibt als Schadensart unkodiert. Maßnahmen: interdisziplinäre Entwicklungsteams, Transparenz und nicht ausschließlich digitaler Erstkontakt, vorgeschlagen. Aufgaben: Chatbots im Erstkontakt und in der Beratung, Entscheidungsunterstützung (MAEWIN, Predictive Analytics) und Forschung (CASoTex, NLP-gestützte Inhaltsanalyse). Theoriebezug als Grenzfall: Staub-Bernasconis Konzept der Menschenrechtsprofession rahmt die Gesamtanalyse und wird in der Diskussion ausdrücklich auf das Diskriminierungsverbot bezogen. Bias-Verständnis nur implizit als Reproduktion vorhandener Kontexte.

Mitigation stage: the work places its intervention at inference ('additional information at inference') with model weights frozen, coded Intra_Processing; the trained parameters are prompt embeddings, not the model, so In_Training is not coded. The intervention changes the model input, coded Prompt_Practice. Evaluated with mixed results (on par with the state of the art, second to INLP on BERT). Axes: gender is the target; race and religion are measured as side effects on StereoSet. fields.AN_Notes: Formal hypercube framework for intersectional fairness with proofs, a variance-based metric family (VarRatio) and verification on synthetic data and the Adult dataset. Studientyp Konzept: the core contribution is the framework, the propagation algorithm and the metrics; the synthetic and real-data experiments serve to verify the theoretical results. Gender, ethnicity and age are the work's own worked examples and the Adult protected attributes (marital status is a further attribute, not coded as a social axis of disadvantage). Indirect_Discrimination: the work defines worst case disparate impact and statistical parity for the outcomes of a binary classification, proves their propagation and finds intersectional bias in Adult; the classification follows the work's own use of disparate impact. Disparate_Performance: section 4.2 and Appendix B extend the framework to Equality of Opportunity, 'that seek to equalize the performance of our model on different subgroups', and prove that worst case accuracy, precision and error-rate disparities narrow up the levels; this rests on the work's own derivation and is not measured empirically. Gender is binary by construction (binary protected attributes, male/female). No mitigation is applied; bottom-up fairness is a design principle without a stage. Theory reference: Crenshaw's intersectionality from Black feminist scholarship frames the problem.

fields.AN_Notes: Edited volume (introduction, sixteen chapters, outlook) coded as one Work; codes collect what individual chapters carry as their own argument or result. Studientyp Theoretisch after the predominantly conceptual chapters; Plafky et al. report own usability tests and a focus group on an LLM case-note prototype, Holz et al. demonstrate classical NLP on a synthetic case, Schlomann draws on the KI-Alter field study. General_Guidance strategy: Plafky et al. instruct a local Mistral 7B with a fixed case-note structure (Wer, Wann, Wo, Grund, Ablauf, Diskussionsinhalte, Vereinbarungen, fachliche Interpretation, Entscheidung, naechster Termin; Tabelle 1), and testers ask for selectable templates per note type; Botzum et al. propose mandatory documentation of the prompts students used. AN_Prompting_Role: Learning_Content from Beranek (prompting as communicative competence), Recommended_Practice from Plafky et al. and Botzum et al., Object_of_Critique from Pelzl's analysis of prompting attacks as a manipulation practice. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender (Beranek's own example list, Schlomann's gendered digital divide), Race_Ethnicity (Steiner on the AFST and ethnically marginalised children), Disability (Steiner's chapter makes AI-related exclusion of disabled people its object and demands models that do not reinforce exclusion 'vor allem im Bereich Behinderung'), Age (Schlomann, age discrimination as own argument), Socioeconomic (editors' Allegheny poverty example, Schlomann on education), Language_Culture (Plafky et al., own observation that Swiss German dialect recognition depends on proximity to Standard German), Nationality_Migration (editors' bias-audit example and the Dutch child-benefit case). Sexual orientation appears only in enumerations. Intersectional not coded: the BIPoC-women facial-recognition result is cited from Buolamwini/Gebru without an own argument that depends on the combination. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms (editors: addressees deviate from the norm dominating internet training data), Erasure (Steiner: data selection and weighting under-represent marginalised discourses and groups; Tappe: AI-generated visual narratives decide which cultural references remain invisible), Disparate_Performance (own observation on dialect recognition, a quality difference between language varieties). Amazon hiring, Dutch child benefit, Allegheny risk scores, UNESCO images and Gender Shades are cited cases and stay uncoded under rule 1.4.1. AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: training-data analysis, exclusion or synthetic data (Pre_Processing) and bias audit, diverse developer teams, ethics boards, human-in-the-loop and staff training (Organisational_Process) are recommended; the AFST evaluation reported by Steiner concerns a decision-support tool's side effect on ethnic disparities, not a tested bias mitigation. AN_Gender_Definition Absent and AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear: gender appears only in short discrimination examples, the cited gender gap of older women and men, and enumerations that also name LGBTQIA+ and queer people; no chapter determines gender, and these signals do not settle a binary or any other understanding. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit (Loehe; Dummann footnote 6; also Rottkemper). AN_Theory_Reference: Steiner frames under-representation and exclusion through a critical conception of inclusion and exclusion (Luhmann, Stichweh) with critical theory and Rojas' radical inclusion concept; Staub-Bernasconi, Media Equation and CASA frame ethics or communication, not gender or bias. Feministisch nein: no feminist theory or method and no structural gender critique.

fields.AN_Notes: Invited paper on ChatGPT in social work research. General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'develop prompts that explicitly ask to identify the work of BIPOC scholars and resources and perspectives from underrepresented communities'; the paper also asks authors to disclose how the LLM was used with prompts. Bias axes from the work's own argument: white-centric content and BIPOC authors (Race_Ethnicity), Eurocentric content, authors from the Global South and mainstream white English (Language_Culture). Gender, sexuality, ability and caste appear only in an enumeration and stay uncoded. Harm types rest on the work's own argument about scraping and ranking of sources: Eurocentric and white-centric content as default (Exclusionary_Norms) and ignored literature of BIPOC and Global South authors (Erasure). Mitigation: inclusive prompting and an ethical framework by the professional organisations, proposed. Task: research uses (research questions, qualitative themes, transcript editing, manuscript feedback); reviewing case notes for biased language is described as a research use. The antiracist research framework (Goings et al. 2023) frames the treatment of bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Policy report on data quality, business models and alternatives for foundation models, addressed in the preface to practitioners and decision-makers of mission-driven organisations including social services and migration counselling. AN_Population General_Social_Work with the caveat that the addressees also include environmental and other common-good organisations. AN_Task Counselling_Client_Communication from chatbots in migration counselling, social benefit advice and crisis hotlines. Bias axes: Language_Culture (American English and majority-culture dominance, low-resource languages) and Socioeconomic (digital divide by design, only the wealthy benefit fully). Gender appears in cited examples (Bolukbasi et al. on 'professor', Wikipedia editors, the Austrian employment-agency chatbot), a pronoun ambiguity remark and the preface only and is not coded as an axis. Physical_Appearance from the report's own uncited worked example of the 'dumb' and 'blonde' association in section 3.3.1. Harm types from the report's own argument: erasure of smaller languages and regional variation, American English as stand-in for global knowledge (Exclusionary_Norms), propagation of majority stereotypes. Disparate_Performance and discrimination are named only through cited cases. Mitigation: deliberate curation and multilingual sources (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning, RLHF and constitutional AI as described alternatives (In_Training), transparency, external evaluation, participation and monitoring by organisations (Organisational_Process), all as recommendations. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit from the report's own determination of bias as partiality toward some groups, ideas or practices, framed as culturally variable. AN_Theory_Reference No: monoculture (Scott 1998), the 3Cs framework and data sovereignty frame data curation and compensation, not the treatment of gender or bias. Studientyp Empirisch from the stated method with expert interviews and comparative system analysis, the report is largely conceptual. AI Agent Review: KI_Sonstige teilweise from the report's own argument on the machine-learning dataset lineage (ImageNet, WordNet) of foundation models and the appendix on ML infrastructures, not from the cited child-protection case. Feministisch nein because 'patriarchal' appears once in the publisher's preface and is not developed. Misrepresentation from the expert-interview finding that regional cultures are decontextualized by outside voices, with the sutra example. AN_Population General_Social_Work follows the explicit addressing of social services in the preface, which the domain experts should confirm, since the main text addresses mission-driven organisations in general.

AN_Task Counselling_Client_Communication from chatbots in migration counselling, social benefit advice and crisis hotlines. Bias axes: Language_Culture (American English and majority-culture dominance, low-resource languages) and Socioeconomic (digital divide by design, only the wealthy benefit fully). Gender appears in cited examples (Bolukbasi et al. on 'professor', Wikipedia editors, the Austrian employment-agency chatbot), a pronoun ambiguity remark and the preface only and is not coded as an axis. Physical_Appearance from the report's own uncited worked example of the 'dumb' and 'blonde' association in section 3.3.1. Harm types from the report's own argument: erasure of smaller languages and regional variation, American English as stand-in for global knowledge (Exclusionary_Norms), propagation of majority stereotypes. Disparate_Performance and discrimination are named only through cited cases. Mitigation: deliberate curation and multilingual sources (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning, RLHF and constitutional AI as described alternatives (In_Training), transparency, external evaluation, participation and monitoring by organisations (Organisational_Process), all as recommendations. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit from the report's own determination of bias as partiality toward some groups, ideas or practices, framed as culturally variable. AN_Theory_Reference No: monoculture (Scott 1998), the 3Cs framework and data sovereignty frame data curation and compensation, not the treatment of gender or bias. fields.AN_Notes: Debiasing framework for text-to-image generation in which a fine-tuned LLM rewrites generic prompts to match target demographic distributions; evaluated against ground-truth ratios and regex and NER baselines. General_Guidance strategy, verbatim: 'transform generic prompts devoid of demographic specifics into those that are demographically informed'. ICL: few-shot prompting of GPT-3 for training data. Mitigation stages: Prompt_Practice for the rewriting of prompts before a frozen image model, and In_Training for the proportional fine-tuning of the rewriting LLM with learning rates scaled by the measured bias per demographic characteristic (section 3.2.4, Algorithms 2 and 3). The work classifies its method as post-processing, but it changes no output of the image model, so Post_Processing is not coded. Status Evaluated: the reduction of the gap between generated and target ratios for ethnicity and gender is reported. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own observation that generic prompts default to White subjects and prioritise certain groups. Gender is analysed as male and female; the limitation sentence that gender should not be confined to the binary does not change the analysis.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only because gender itself is not defined. AN_Task None: general LLM bias survey without an application task.

fields.AN_Notes: Interviewstudie (25 Teilnehmende) mit vorab erzeugten ChatGPT-Antworten auf vier Prompts, in denen person durch man, woman, non-binary person ersetzt wird. Prompts dienen als Forschungsinstrument und als vorgeschlagene Test-Suite; die Ersetzung des Personenbegriffs ist keine Technik der Prompt-Report-Familien, daher AN_Prompt_Techniques None. Sexual_Orientation_Identity codiert, weil nicht-binäre und trans Personen als eigene Analysegruppe geführt werden (Geschlechtsidentität); das Werk nennt die Achse gender, daher beide Werte. Schadensarten aus der eigenen Output-Analyse (3.1) und den Interviewbefunden (4.6.2): Stereotyping, cis-zentrischer Default (Exclusionary_Norms), Reduktion nicht-binärer Figuren auf Identitätskämpfe (Misrepresentation). Tonunterschiede nicht als Disparate_Performance codiert (Codebuch 1.4.1), wahrgenommene Genauigkeit gleich über Gruppen. Maßnahmen nur vorgeschlagen: diversere Trainingsdaten und Co-Design bei der Datenkuratierung (Pre_Processing), Rückfragen des Modells bei vagen Prompts (Intra_Processing, 5.2.2), Co-Design, Prompt-Test-Suite und Echtzeit- sowie Community-Bias-Auditing (Organisational_Process). Grounded Theory und reflexive thematische Analyse sind Methoden, keine Theorie, die Gender oder Bias rahmt.

Sexual_Orientation_Identity codiert, weil nicht-binäre und trans Personen als eigene Analysegruppe geführt werden (Geschlechtsidentität); das Werk nennt die Achse gender, daher beide Werte. Schadensarten aus der eigenen Output-Analyse (3.1) und den Interviewbefunden (4.6.2): Stereotyping, cis-zentrischer Default (Exclusionary_Norms), Reduktion nicht-binärer Figuren auf Identitätskämpfe (Misrepresentation). Tonunterschiede nicht als Disparate_Performance codiert (Codebuch 1.4.1), wahrgenommene Genauigkeit gleich über Gruppen. Maßnahmen nur vorgeschlagen: diversere Trainingsdaten und Co-Design bei der Datenkuratierung (Pre_Processing), Rückfragen des Modells bei vagen Prompts (Intra_Processing, 5.2.2), Co-Design, Prompt-Test-Suite und Echtzeit- sowie Community-Bias-Auditing (Organisational_Process). Grounded Theory und reflexive thematische Analyse sind Methoden, keine Theorie, die Gender oder Bias rahmt.

fields.AN_Notes: Konzeptionelles Policy-Paper der Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung, das Feminist AI als Rahmen vorschlägt. Bias-Achse Geschlecht als eigenes Argument (männlich dominierte Verzerrungen, binäre Geschlechterkategorien schließen nicht-binäre Personen aus). Ethnizität, Klasse, Alter und weitere Kategorien stehen nur in der Bestimmung von Intersektionalität und in der Aufzählung der MIRA-Metriken, keine Passage macht ein Ergebnis von einer Achsenkombination abhängig, daher kein Intersectional. Schadensart Exclusionary_Norms aus dem eigenen Prüfkriterium zu binären Kategorien, die strukturelle Diskriminierung und das maskulinistische Intelligenzverständnis sind zitiert. Maßnahmen: Prüfung von Trainingsdaten auf Diversität und synthetische Trainingsdaten bei MIRA (Pre_Processing), diverse Teams, Stakeholder-Beteiligung, Feminist Design Tool, Gesetzgebung und Wartungszyklen (Organisational_Process). Demonstrated bezieht sich allein auf MIRA als umgesetztes und vorgestelltes Beispiel ohne berichtete Evaluation, die übrigen Maßnahmen bleiben Vorschläge. Other_Task: medizinische Diagnostik im MIRA-Praxisbeispiel. Handlungsfeld bleibt Not_SW_Specific, weil das Werk KI allgemein adressiert und Gesundheit nur das Feld eines Beispiels ist. Social_Construct aus der Bestimmung des Patriarchats als Machtsystem, in dem Männer Macht halten. Die Kritik binärer Geschlechterkategorien ist ein Gestaltungsprinzip ohne nicht-binäre Analysekategorie, daher kein Non_Binary_Inclusive. Gender wird nicht in einem eigenen Satz bestimmt. Bias-Verständnis nur implizit über systemische Machtstrukturen als Ursache von Ungleichheit. Das MIRA-Beispiel beruht nach eigener Angabe auf einem Interview mit dem Start-up.

fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review of AI and machine learning in social work: predictive risk analytics in child welfare, mental-health chatbots, NLP for case notes, automated case management, AI in social work education. AN_Bias_Axes Race_Ethnicity: the review develops the over-representation of families from certain ethnic backgrounds in child-abuse risk prediction as its own worked example (4.1) and returns to the Allegheny case (4.1.1). Socioeconomic (housing vouchers, Turner et al. 2020, absent from the reference list) and Language_Culture (English-only chatbots) appear only as single-sentence cited cases in 4.1.1, and gender only in the enumeration 'racial, gender, or socio-economic disparities', so they stay uncoded. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination: the review's own argument in 4.1 places the disadvantage in risk scores learned from historical data that affect access to services and child welfare interventions, an allocation through biased data rather than the attribute itself; the work does not classify the discrimination. Mitigation Proposed: diverse and inclusive datasets (Pre_Processing); auditing, transparency, involvement of social workers and community members, AI training (Organisational_Process); none is assessed. AN_Task: predictive risk assessment (Case_Assessment_Decision_Support), mental-health chatbots (Counselling_Client_Communication), NLP summaries of case notes and automated documentation (Documentation_Recording), AI tools and AI-driven personalised learning in social work education and training (Teaching_Further_Education, Sections 5.3.3 and 6.1.1). Source quality: several in-text citations do not match the reference list, for example 'Baker et al., 2021' cited for NLP documentation while reference [3] is a review of AI in net-zero building design, 'Chukwunweike et al.' cited for predictive analytics in social work while reference [9] concerns loop execution in deep-learning systems, and 'Turner et al., 2020' absent from the list; this limits the evidential weight of the cited case studies without changing the publication type.

fields.AN_Notes: Book chapter (Feminist AI volume) on the gender relations of digitalisation: missing women in AI, masculinity and technical expertise, technoculture, AI feedback loops. Intersectional rests on the own review of workforce data, women of colour particularly under-represented. Harms from the own argument: masculine defaults and masculine preferences inscribed in AI (Exclusionary_Norms) and the gender data gap as failure to collect data on women (Erasure); the cited cases (Amazon hiring, chatbot hate speech, mask recognition, word embeddings) are not coded separately. Mitigation: more women and diverse teams in AI, recruitment and leadership policies, proposed as remedy for the feedback loop; the Carnegie Mellon and Harvey Mudd figures concern women in computer science, not an evaluated bias measure in AI. Technical debiasing is judged insufficient. Fairness teilweise as critique of fairness metrics.

Grenzfall, weil der Fall aus der Literatur übernommen ist. Bias wird über strukturelle Ungleichheit und differenzielle Wirkungen gerahmt, ohne eigene Bestimmung. fields.AN_Notes: Commentary with seven recommended actions for social change leaders and ML developers, grounded in the authors' tracking of publicly reported biased AI systems at the Berkeley Haas Center for Equity, Gender and Leadership. AN_Task Other_Task: credit-limit assessment and candidate ranking as worked examples, plus civil society use of ML for financial inclusion. Bias axes Gender and Race_Ethnicity from the own system analysis ('both gender and racial bias') and the credit example ('along gender ( and race ) lines'). Intersectional not coded, the darker-skinned women example from Gender Shades compares the extreme groups only and is cited. Non-binary persons are treated within the Gender axis, the separation from Sexual_Orientation_Identity is an open rule question. Harm types structure the own impact analysis: lower quality of service (Disparate_Performance), stereotype reinforcement, erasure of marginalised gender identities, male bodies as medical standard (Exclusionary_Norms). Indirect_Discrimination from the Gild proxy 'social data' that ranks female candidates lower. The 'unfair allocation of resources' category of the own analysis is allocative without a direct or indirect classification and is covered only through the Gild example. Mitigation: feminist data practices, dataset assessment and documentation (Pre_Processing), team diversity, AI literacy training, gender-sensitive governance, algorithm audits and participatory design (Organisational_Process), all recommended. AN_Gender_Understanding Non_Binary_Inclusive because the own impact analysis counts women and non-binary individuals as affected groups. Social_Construct not coded, the text criticises the binary classification but does not state that gender is socially produced. Theory reference Data Feminism frames the recommended treatment of gender data gaps. AI Agent Review: Derogatory_Language is not coded. The own impact category 'derogatory and offensive treatment or erasure of already marginalized gender identities' names treatment rather than language, and its only illustration, binary gender classification in facial analysis, establishes Erasure.

ReGiFT extracts SQuAD-v2 traces and retains only final-answer-correct examples (3.1, Algorithm 1: Pre_Processing); section 6 assesses Correct-Only, Incorrect-Only and Full-Set selection. Supervised fine-tuning jointly teaches traces and answers (3.2: In_Training). Section 5.2 and Table 3 assess a CoT prompting comparator (Prompt_Practice) and criticise prompt sensitivity and demographic generalisation. Prompting is Research_Instrument and Object_of_Critique. Thought_Generation comprises CoT and explicit think/answer prompts. General_Guidance, verbatim A.1: Answer each question using the information in the preceding background paragraph. If there is not enough information provided, answer with ‘Not in background.’ A.1 explicitly excludes demonstrations in the zero-shot prompt; no ICL. The abstention/context guidance is used, but its isolated mitigation efficacy is not tested. Evaluated denotes completed ReGiFT, data-selection, instruction-tuning and CoT intervention assessments with reported results, not universal effectiveness. Tables 1–3 report ReGiFT gains relative to base models on BBQ; CoT outcomes are mixed or negative. Age, Religion and Nationality_Migration are the three separately evaluated axes (4.1, 5; no interacting-axis analysis). Stereotyping is the explicit harm (Figures 1/3, A.5); demographic benchmark scenarios do not establish a social-work or professional-education setting. Study type Experimentell; population Not_SW_Specific; Fulltext plus all three original PNGs. Answer extraction, Unknown normalisation and LLM-as-Judge serve measurement (4.3, A.2–A.3); they do not establish Post_Processing, Intra_Processing or Organisational_Process mitigation. Correct final answers are an admitted proxy for trace validity (3.1 footnote), not direct verification of reasoning correctness. The paper limits its claim to stereotypes associated with flawed contextual reasoning and mid-sized models, without complete bias removal or demonstrated transfer to social-work practice. Numerical limitations: Tables 1 and 3 disagree on Mistral ReGiFT age (82.78/84.01 versus 82.58/83.91) and Phi-4 religion/nationality entries; section 5.2 overgeneralises CoT as modest gains. Several displayed overall entries also do not equal the mean of displayed ambiguous/disambiguous entries (e.g. Table 1 LLaMA base religion 12.45/66.52/49.48 and Table 4 Correct-Only age 70.04/89.13/75.59); the paper supplies no reconciliation. Table 5 is nonmonotonic and does not substantiate a universal 40% plateau; its prose mentions 50% although no 50% row is shown. Figure 4 shows printed means 139.62 and 243.81 tokens with undefined error bars and unspecified sample sizes; no confidence interval, statistical significance, trace-length causal effect or operational threshold is inferred. These limitations restrict quantitative synthesis, but the topical coding and completed-assessment status remain decidable.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper mapping Long and Magerko's AI literacy framework onto the nine CSWE core competencies. Bias axes come from the authors' own worked examples: a mortgage denial that ignores informal income (Socioeconomic) and a mental-health agency model trained on English-speaking insured clients (Language_Culture, Socioeconomic); race and disability appear only in enumerations and cited cases. Harm types: the lending example is an allocation in which an apparently neutral criterion disadvantages the family (Indirect_Discrimination); the agency example makes the dominant client group the default and overlooks marginalised groups (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation is recommended only: advocacy for more inclusive data (Pre_Processing) and human review, appeals, community forums, training and governance (Organisational_Process). Tasks are named as AI uses in practice: summarising case histories and drafting reports, risk and needs identification, chatbots and drafting client communication, scheduling and data entry, research uses of LLMs, classroom use. The AI literacy framework frames competencies, not the treatment of bias, so AN_Theory_Reference is No; 'antiracist and intersectional lenses' appear only as a recommendation in Table 2.
