fields.AN_Notes: Systematic review of 67 social work AI articles with a proposed Unified Model of Artificial Intelligence Enhanced Social Work along Staub-Bernasconi's triple mandate. Child welfare is the dominant practice area of the reviewed literature (RQ1a), while the model addresses social work in general, so AN_Population is General_Social_Work. Bias axes: indigenous peoples, younger people and the poor appear only as an enumeration of cited under- or over-represented groups, so None. Harm types: the synthesis theme Data and Algorithmic Injustice names exclusion, invisibility, stigmatisation and discrimination as cited consequences without structuring them as harm types, so None. AN_Task: decision support and predictive risk assessment (profession level), text mining for social work research, and agency resource allocation and data exchange (Administration). Mitigation proposals: inclusive data sets (Pre_Processing) and governance, oversight, participation, training and interdisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process). Bias is not defined; its understanding follows the human-rights principle of nondiscrimination. AI Agent Review: AN_Harm_Types None. The synthesis theme 'Data and Algorithmic Injustice' is a section of the review, but it is organised as injustice in general and lists consequences (exclusion, injustice, prejudices, stigmatization and discrimination, invisibility) each taken from a cited study; no harm type structures the synthesis as a section, table row or coded category, and the groups concerned stand in an enumeration that also leaves AN_Bias_Axes at None.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

fields.AN_Notes: Reflective empirical account of the co-creation workshops of the Horizon Europe MAMMOth project with marginalised groups (women at risk of social exclusion, young people, ethnic minorities, migrants, LGBTQI+ early career researchers), each opened by a training module on AI bias, feeding user and research requirements of an AI bias toolkit. Mitigation Demonstrated: the training within co-creation was applied and is reported only through facilitator and participant reflections, without a completed assessment of an effect on AI bias, although the work calls its approach an evaluation. AN_Task Other_Task: AI-based home loan decisions, biometric identity verification and academic citation search as use cases, outside social work. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender through the training examples added by DAF (generative AI answers on fathers and mothers, gendered job endings in Google Translate, Section 5.1); Religion and Physical_Appearance through the ranked facial attributes for identity verification (hijabs and turbans, piercings and tattoos, Section 4.1). Race_Ethnicity stays uncoded: postal codes as proxy of race appear only as a parenthetical example of a toolkit challenge (Section 4) and the participant consensus that white males benefit most from credit scoring is a single reported perception (Section 4.2); the enumeration 'gender, age, ethnic origin, and sexual orientation' and the participant groups are not coded either. AN_Harm_Types: Stereotyping from the gender-role examples demonstrated in the training, Indirect_Discrimination from the proxy bias the project's own toolkit is built to address. Gender is treated through examples only, without a stated or recognisable understanding, hence Absent and Unclear. AN_Theory_Reference Yes: critical and social-justice perspectives on participatory design (power relations, 'box-ticking', ethics-washing) frame the treatment of AI bias and training; boundary between framing tradition and methodological label. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise: participants include recipients of social protection services and domestic violence victims recruited via civil society organisations, but no social work practice is addressed. The Markdown conversion duplicates and scrambles parts of Sections 4.3 to 5.3; all quotes come from coherent passages.

fields.AN_Notes: Experiments on the emotional content of responses of seven LLMs to heteronormative versus non-heteronormative prompts and to LGBTQ+ slang. Axes: queer identity expressed through language (Sexual_Orientation_Identity) and queer slang as a language variety, 'minority slangs and argots' (Language_Culture). The more negative emotion labels for queer slang are a difference in tone and are therefore not coded as Disparate_Performance; Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own result and argument that guardrails against heteronormative language leave a bias against queer language. Bias definition: the adopted Vasquez definition determines heteronormative language as the input category of the experiments; LLM bias itself is recognisable only from the measurement of disproportionately negative emotional labels, so Implicit_Only. Existing safety guardrails are inferred from response patterns and are not an identified or assessed mitigation, so mitigation is None. Gender understanding: the heteronormativity frame treats traditional gender roles, binary gender norms and cisnormativity as normative orders encoded in language, which is taken as the explicit statement for Social_Construct; this is a boundary case under codebook 1.4.1 and is flagged. fields.AN_Notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only because gender itself is not defined. AN_Task None: general LLM bias survey without an application task.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only because gender itself is not defined. AN_Task None: general LLM bias survey without an application task.

Race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation und gender expression stehen nur in Aufzählungen geschützter Kategorien, daher AN_Bias_Axes None. AN_Harm_Types: nicht entscheidbar aus Fulltext. Das Werk argumentiert in eigenen Worten eine verzerrte Beurteilung von Klient:innen durch nicht repräsentative Trainingsdaten, also eine Entscheidung über Personen, ordnet sie aber weder als unmittelbare noch als mittelbare Diskriminierung ein und nennt kein Kriterium und kein stellvertretendes Merkmal. Vorgeschlagene Maßnahmen sind die Datenbehandlung zur Bias-Reduktion (Pre_Processing) sowie Ethik-Steuerungskomitee, diverse Fokusgruppen, Peer Review von Algorithmen, Simulationen, Schulung und Testprotokoll (Organisational_Process). AN_Task folgt den im Werk beschriebenen Einsätzen, nämlich KI-gestützte Beurteilung und Diagnostik, Kommunikation mit Klient:innen über KI, ChatGPT für Förderanträge und Fundraising sowie der KI-gestützte Crisis Contact Simulator zur Schulung von Beratenden. Bias wird über nicht repräsentative Daten und Ungleichbehandlung geschützter Gruppen erkennbar, aber nicht bestimmt. Die Ethikstandards sind kein Theoriebezug.

fields.AN_Notes: Theoretical essay applying intersectionality, Black feminist thought, queer theory and critical race theory to AI. Race is developed through the risk-assessment example the work frames as the New Jim Code and through Black feminist and POC community strategies; trans, bisexual and femme communities enter as categories of the argument (conceptual, not measured). The ProPublica and ImageNet harms are cited cases and stay uncoded; age, disability and ableism appear only in a cited quotation. The work's own argument is that normative algorithmic categorisation constrains identities that are not easily categorised (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation: intersectional strategies at data, design and implementation stages, community methodologies and the Data Nutrition Label as a data-collection example, proposed. Other_Task: artistic and tactical media practice with AI (the ladymouth chatbot, natural language processing in poetic practice). Gender definition coded Explicit through the adopted queer-theory determination that female is not a clearly defined natural category.

fields.AN_Notes: Systematic review of nine implementation studies of predictive risk tools in child welfare, structured by CFIR and the ethical evaluation frameworks of Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020). AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated is a synthesised evaluation, not the review's own experiment: the review reports that the post-processing fairness correction of Purdy and Glass (2023), group-specific risk thresholds, reduced false positive and false negative error rates among four subgroups; it also reports the racial equity report of Putnam-Hornstein et al. (2022) finding comparable accuracy across racial and ethnic groups. Other mitigation stages remain description or recommendation: exclusion of bias-prone variables after community consultation and feature selection (Pre_Processing), stakeholder consensus, training against automation bias and external ethics reviews (Organisational_Process). Race_Ethnicity is the axis of the synthesised subgroup analyses, thresholds and equity reports; gender is mentioned once as a subgroup dimension of accuracy checks and socioeconomic status only in a cited discussion sentence, so both stay uncoded. Harm types follow the review's own synthesis: subgroup error rates and equity in subgroups as Disparate_Performance, historical bias in administrative records and racial disparities in screening outcomes as Indirect_Discrimination. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit rests on the adopted equity criterion of Russell (2015), 'equity evaluates whether predictions function consistently across subgroups'. AN_Theory_Reference No (resolved by the AI Agent Review): Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020) are evaluation criteria and a practical framework that the review uses as an assessment checklist, and CFIR is an implementation framework; the review itself names the limited use of theoretical frameworks as a gap and mentions feminist and other critical theories only as a future-research suggestion. fields.AN_Notes: Philosophischer Beitrag: AI bias als strukturelle Ungerechtigkeit nach Iris Marion Young, Fallbeispiel Gesundheitsversorgung entlang von vier Entwicklungsstufen. Bias-Achsen aus der eigenen Stufenanalyse: race (Hautkrebsdaten, Kostenproxy, VBAC), gender (gender research gap) und class oder Einkommen (10/90 gap, EHR-Verfügbarkeit, Versicherung). Schadensarten aus der eigenen Stufenanalyse in Abschnitt 3.2, die zitierte Fälle als Belege des eigenen Arguments ausführt: Disparate_Performance (schiefe Daten, bessere Leistung für hellhäutige Personen), Direct_Discrimination (Race als Input des VBAC-Scores), Indirect_Discrimination (Gesundheitskosten als Proxy für Bedarf, ZIP-Code). Die Anerkennungs- und Repräsentationsbeispiele in 4.1 (Menstruations-App nach Eveleth, Suchmaschine nach Noble) illustrieren nur die begriffliche Erweiterung über Ressourcenverteilung hinaus und bleiben nach Codebuch 1.4.1 als zitierte Fälle uncodiert. Evaluated beschränkt sich auf die synthetisierte Studie von Pierson et al. (2021): patientenberichtete Schmerzwerte als Label und diverser Datensatz (Pre_Processing) senken unerklärte Schmerzdisparitäten; keine eigene Evaluation. Übrige Empfehlungen (Table 1, Minipublics, Beteiligung Marginalisierter, Monitoring) bleiben Vorschläge. AN_Task Other_Task: klinische Diagnose und Bedarfsschätzung in der Medizin. Gender als teilweiser Gegenstand ohne bestimmbares Verständnis, daher Absent und Unclear.

fields.AN_Notes: Interpretative qualitative visual analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (poverty/wealth, criminal/law enforcement, immigrant/citizen, worker/executive, ideologies, everyday scenarios), followed by a micro, meso and macro intersectional analysis. Prompting is a research instrument; the recommendation that users be more conscious of the prompts they use is Recommended_Practice without a codable technique, so AN_Prompt_Techniques is None. Language_Culture covers cultural context and Global North hegemony in depictions of food and settings; Physical_Appearance covers body size and conventional attractiveness. Mitigation proposals: better curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), and algorithmic reparation, regulation, criminal culpability and diverse development teams (Organisational_Process); all proposed. Studientyp Empirisch rather than Experimentell because the prompt contrasts serve an interpretative analysis without a controlled comparison. The confederate flag is discussed as violent imagery, but Toxicity is not coded because the codebook ties it to language. AN_Task None because the work audits a general image generator without a professional application task. AI Agent Review: AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only: the passages after Guillaumin and on intersectionality determine power systems and the interplay of oppressions, not bias or discrimination, and the work sets 'biases' in quotation marks without determining it. Fairness teilweise rests on the recommendations structured around algorithmic reparation as a foundation for building, evaluating and adjusting machine learning systems, with deliberate intervention and training data curation, a subordinate treatment of fair system design.

fields.AN_Notes: Audit study with 42 prompt templates in five scenarios (purchase, chess, public office, sports, hiring) and 40 first names perceived as Black or white and male or female, 100 repetitions each, on GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Mistral Large and PaLM-2. Prompts are the research instrument, and the three context levels test prompt design. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'providing the model with a numeric anchor' (decision-relevant numeric information in the prompt), which the work's own experiment shows to remove name-based disparities in most scenarios, while qualitative context has inconsistent effects (Prompt_Practice, Evaluated); routine audits at deployment and implementation are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed). Other_Task: advice to laypeople in negotiation, hiring salary offers, election and sports predictions, outside social work. Intersectional is coded under the AN_Bias_Axes rule because Black female-perceived names yield the worst outcomes compared with Black and with female names, although the authors state that this analysis does not equate to an evaluation of intersectionality. Harm type: Indirect_Discrimination following the codebook anchor, since names act as proxies in numeric advice about persons (offers, salaries, chances) and the work interprets the disparities as disparate impact. The outputs are allocative decisions, not depictions of groups, and the encoded stereotypes are the authors' explanation of the mechanism; Stereotyping is therefore not coded as a separate representational harm. Gender is operationalised through male- and female-perceived names without definition. Bias is defined through the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact, which also frames the interpretation (theory reference, a boundary case between legal doctrine and theory).

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

fields.AN_Notes: Practice guide for managers and staff in small and medium enterprises with the KI-FAIRNESS prompting framework, organisational measures and own image-prompt trials in DALL-E 2 and Midjourney. Publication type admitted as scholarly grey literature (university publisher, named authorship, source list, expert contributions), flagged for the domain experts. Other_Task: drafting job advertisements, recommendation letters and company images in HR and marketing. General_Guidance strategy, verbatim: 'Es könnte z.B. explizit gefordert werden, dass Frauen und Männer, Menschen unterschiedlicher Hautfarbe und sozialer Schicht dargestellt werden sollen.' Further strategies: choose the context deliberately, prompt in English ('female and male bosses'), weigh neutrality against explicit diversity, omit gender in recommendation letters or use a 'Verwirrungstaktik', anonymise. Bias axes and harm types rest on the guide's own image-prompt observations and its own job-advertisement argument (Indirect_Discrimination: job-advertisement language that appeals to men deters women and is perpetuated by training); cited news cases are not used. Mitigation status Evaluated applies only to adding 'divers' to the prompt, whose effect is tested in two tools and reported as small; the trial is informal (one prompt), and the other measures (data diversity, targeted training with gender-inclusive terms, governance, training of staff, monitoring, human review) are proposed. Gender understanding: the image analysis contrasts women and men, so Binary_Categorical follows the analysis; the Gender Data Gap remark on genderqueer people, the gender star and 'alle Gender' are conceptual statements that the analysis does not follow. Intersectional rests on the guide's own statement that women and especially Women of Color are sexualised in generated images. Theory reference No: 'Feministische KI' appears only in the outlook as a positive narrative with the MissJourney example, and Data Feminism and the Gender Data Gap appear as further reading or illustration; none of them frames the guide's treatment of gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Practice guide for managers and staff in small and medium enterprises with the KI-FAIRNESS prompting framework, organisational measures and own image-prompt trials in DALL-E 2 and Midjourney. Publication type admitted as scholarly grey literature (university publisher, named authorship, source list, expert contributions), flagged for the domain experts. Other_Task: drafting job advertisements, recommendation letters and company images in HR and marketing. General_Guidance strategy, verbatim: 'Es könnte z.B. explizit gefordert werden, dass Frauen und Männer, Menschen unterschiedlicher Hautfarbe und sozialer Schicht dargestellt werden sollen.' Further strategies: choose the context deliberately, prompt in English ('female and male bosses'), weigh neutrality against explicit diversity, omit gender in recommendation letters or use a 'Verwirrungstaktik', anonymise. Bias axes and harm types rest on the guide's own image-prompt observations and its own job-advertisement argument (Indirect_Discrimination: job-advertisement language that appeals to men deters women and is perpetuated by training); cited news cases are not used. Mitigation status Evaluated applies only to adding 'divers' to the prompt, whose effect is tested in two tools and reported as small; the trial is informal (one prompt), and the other measures (data diversity, targeted training with gender-inclusive terms, governance, training of staff, monitoring, human review) are proposed. Gender understanding: the image analysis contrasts women and men, so Binary_Categorical follows the analysis; the Gender Data Gap remark on genderqueer people, the gender star and 'alle Gender' are conceptual statements that the analysis does not follow. Intersectional rests on the guide's own statement that women and especially Women of Color are sexualised in generated images. Theory reference No: 'Feministische KI' appears only in the outlook as a positive narrative with the MissJourney example, and Data Feminism and the Gender Data Gap appear as further reading or illustration; none of them frames the guide's treatment of gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Prompt audit of GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and GPT-4o with regular and flipped Likert-scale prompts on willingness to rent to, work with, marry into the family of, live next to or entrust children to American or North Korean persons with six mental-disability conditions (bipolar disorder, depression, schizophrenia, remitted and symptomatic), plus requested explanations. Mental disability is coded as Disability, the axis the work names; the intersection is nationality with mental disability, without gender. The scenarios elicit attitudes, not decisions about persons, so no discrimination type is coded and the harms are representational. Bias is measured as rating differences and the authors call its interpretation subjective, hence Implicit_Only. The intersectional lens combines nationality and mental disability without a power or gender analysis, so Feministisch stays nein. The mitigation is a future-work recommendation to represent a spectrum of mental disability symptoms in training data. No social work setting.

fields.AN_Notes: Vorschlag eines EPAS-Kompetenzindikators mit vier Fertigkeiten für das MSW-Curriculum. Prompting ist Lerninhalt (Fertigkeit 2) und empfohlene Praxis. Thought_Generation (Chain of Thought) und Role_Persona (Personas aus dem Prompt-Pattern-Katalog nach White et al.) sind als zu vermittelnde Techniken genannt. General_Guidance steht für das iterative Vorgehen 'The tasks of prompting and validating are often iterative'. Bias-Achsen und Schadensbeispiele (Bias gegenüber Frauen, People of Color, sexuell und geschlechtlich minorisierten Personen, CEO-Bilder, race-based medicine) sind zitierte Befunde anderer Arbeiten und nicht als eigene Analyse codiert, Geschlecht ist daher kein Gegenstand. Organisational_Process ist die vorgeschlagene Ausbildungsmaßnahme, Studierende sollen Ausgaben auf Bias prüfen und Minderung diskutieren. AN_Task folgt den im Werk beschriebenen Einsätzen, nämlich Behandlungspläne und Fallnotizen (Documentation_Recording), Materialien für Einzel- und Gruppensitzungen und Übersetzungen (Counselling_Client_Communication), Förderanträge und Fundraising (Administration), Schulungsmaterialien für die Fortbildung (Teaching_Further_Education) sowie die Zusammenfassung von Policy-Dokumenten und Entwürfe von Advocacy-Material auf Makroebene (Other_Task, Policy-Analyse und Advocacy). Bias wird nur als Spiegel der Trainingsdaten erkennbar.

fields.AN_Notes: Higher-education framework of the Open University for staff and students under an EDIA lens. General_Guidance strategies, verbatim: 'engage in equitable and inclusive prompting when required', 'Use the same/different prompt(s) several times with the same/different tool(s) and compare the outputs to identify and mitigate potential (cultural) bias.', 'Engage in a conversation with AI to challenge detected biases.' and 'prompting for inclusivity'. The comparison of outputs serves bias detection and is not combined into one answer, so Ensembling is not coded. Bias axes appear only in an enumeration (gender, cultural, disability, racial), so no axis is coded. Epistemic injustice and the non-inclusive nature of outputs are asserted as premises without a mechanism the framework itself develops, so no harm type is coded. Mitigation: inclusive prompting practice and embedding Critical AI Literacy in curricula and staff development, proposed. Critical Digital Literacy and epistemic injustice frame the treatment of bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Experiment mit fünf LLMs auf StereoSet und GenAssocBias, Messgröße ist die Rate stereotyper Antworten. General_Guidance steht für die System-2-Anweisung 'You answer questions slowly and thoughtfully. Your answers are effortful and reliable.', Thought_Generation für 'Let's think step-by-step', Role_Persona für 'Adopt the identity of a person/machine'. Evaluiert wird die eigene Prompt-Intervention, Human Persona mit System 2 senkt stereotype Antworten im Mittel am stärksten, CoT erhöht sie in jedem Minimalpaar. Bias-Achsen nach den gemessenen Kategorien, Beauty als Physical_Appearance. Die Kategorien profession, beauty in profession und institutional bleiben uncodiert, weil Beruf und Institution keine Achse sozialer Benachteiligung im Sinne der Liste sind und Other_Axis keine nicht-soziale Variable aufnimmt. Gender ist eine von neun Messkategorien ohne Bestimmung des Begriffs. Theoriebezug ist die Dual-Process-Theorie, die die Entstehung sozialer Bias im Modell rahmt.

fields.AN_Notes: Feministische Policy-Analyse von sieben internationalen AI-Safety-Initiativen mit einem eigenen Bewertungsraster (vier Ziele mit je drei Fragen, Punktwerte je Initiative). Die Achsen stammen aus dem eigenen Argument gegen eine vermeintlich universelle Bedrohung im Befund zu combat neutrality, nämlich eine einkommensschwache Familie, die durch einen diskriminierenden Algorithmus Sozialleistungen verliert (Socioeconomic), sowie ländliche und indigene Gemeinschaften ohne Wasserzugang durch Rechenzentren (Race_Ethnicity für indigen, Other_Axis für den Wohnort im ländlichen Raum). Geschlecht steht nur in Aufzählungen, im Intersektionalitätsbegriff und im zitierten UN-Text, daher keine Gender-Achse. Intersektionalität ist Rahmen und Bewertungsziel, ein Ergebnis, das von einer Achsenkombination abhängt, fehlt, daher weder Intersectional in AN_Bias_Axes noch in AN_Gender_Understanding. Exclusionary_Norms folgt aus dem eigenen Befund, dass die Initiativen eine universelle, neutrale Sicht auf Risiko setzen und Erfahrungen marginalisierter Gruppen auslassen. Das Wohlfahrtsbeispiel ist eine allokative Benachteiligung, die das Werk weder als unmittelbare noch als mittelbare Diskriminierung einordnet, und bleibt ohne Diskriminierungscode. Vorgeschlagene Maßnahmen sind Audits mit dem Framework, Rechenschaftspflicht von Unternehmen, Beteiligung marginalisierter Gruppen, Bürger:innenjurys und digitale Literacy (Organisational_Process). Geschlecht wird nicht bestimmt, und das Werk sagt nicht selbst, dass Geschlecht sozial hergestellt oder eine Machtstruktur ist. Die Wendung 'gendered systems of oppression' beschreibt den Zweck des übernommenen Rahmens nach McPhail, daher nach der Schwelle von 1.4.1 kein Social_Construct, sondern Unclear mit Absent. Bias wird als Reproduktion sozialer Ungleichheit und Machtverhältnisse gerahmt, aber nicht bestimmt, die Crenshaw-Passage bestimmt Intersektionalität und nicht Bias. Theorien sind Intersektionalität nach Crenshaw, das Feminist Policy Analysis Framework nach McPhail und Data Feminism nach D'Ignazio und Klein.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper mapping Long and Magerko's AI literacy framework onto the nine CSWE core competencies. Bias axes come from the authors' own worked examples: a mortgage denial that ignores informal income (Socioeconomic) and a mental-health agency model trained on English-speaking insured clients (Language_Culture, Socioeconomic); race and disability appear only in enumerations and cited cases. Harm types: the lending example is an allocation in which an apparently neutral criterion disadvantages the family (Indirect_Discrimination); the agency example makes the dominant client group the default and overlooks marginalised groups (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation is recommended only: advocacy for more inclusive data (Pre_Processing) and human review, appeals, community forums, training and governance (Organisational_Process). Tasks are named as AI uses in practice: summarising case histories and drafting reports, risk and needs identification, chatbots and drafting client communication, scheduling and data entry, research uses of LLMs, classroom use. The AI literacy framework frames competencies, not the treatment of bias, so AN_Theory_Reference is No; 'antiracist and intersectional lenses' appear only as a recommendation in Table 2.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper mapping Long and Magerko's AI literacy framework onto the nine CSWE core competencies. Bias axes come from the authors' own worked examples: a mortgage denial that ignores informal income (Socioeconomic) and a mental-health agency model trained on English-speaking insured clients (Language_Culture, Socioeconomic); race and disability appear only in enumerations and cited cases. Harm types: the lending example is an allocation in which an apparently neutral criterion disadvantages the family (Indirect_Discrimination); the agency example makes the dominant client group the default and overlooks marginalised groups (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation is recommended only: advocacy for more inclusive data (Pre_Processing) and human review, appeals, community forums, training and governance (Organisational_Process). Tasks are named as AI uses in practice: summarising case histories and drafting reports, risk and needs identification, chatbots and drafting client communication, scheduling and data entry, research uses of LLMs, classroom use. The AI literacy framework frames competencies, not the treatment of bias, so AN_Theory_Reference is No; 'antiracist and intersectional lenses' appear only as a recommendation in Table 2.

fields.AN_Notes: Fallstudie der Organisation Queer in AI mit eigenen Mitglieder- und Empfängerbefragungen. Die in Abschnitt 2 gelisteten AI-Schäden (Outing, Hassrede, Zensur) sind zitiert; die eigene Analyse betrifft den Ausschluss queerer Menschen aus AI-Forschung, Konferenzen und Publikationswesen. Bias-Achsen, die die eigene Analyse der Teilhabebarrieren entwickelt: gender and sexual orientation (trans und nicht-binäre Personen als eigene Kategorien, Deadnaming), Einkommen (Bewerbungsgebühren, low-income scholars), Global South und Visa (Nationality_Migration), Behinderung und Neurodivergenz, Verstärkung bei intersecting identities. Race_Ethnicity erscheint nur in Demografie- und Reichweitenangaben, Kaste nur in einer Aufzählung (class or caste) und einem Paneltitel; beide bleiben uncodiert. Schadensarten aus eigenen Beobachtungen: exklusive Geschlechtsabfragen und Klarnamenzwang bei Konferenzregistrierung (Exclusionary_Norms), Chat-Software blockiert queere Begriffe (Erasure). Evaluated beschränkt sich auf die organisatorischen Maßnahmen der Organisation (Stipendienprogramm, Workshops, Konferenzleitfaden, Name-Check-Tool), deren Wirkung das Werk nach eigener Angabe bewertet (assess the organization's impact) und mit Befragungsergebnissen und Adoptionsstand berichtet, darunter das gemischte Ergebnis relatively modest adoption; es handelt sich um Maßnahmen gegen Ausschluss aus der AI-Forschung, nicht um technische Bias-Mitigation. Kein ausdrückliches Gender- oder Bias-Verständnis formuliert, Umfragekategorien führen nicht-binäre und weitere Geschlechter.

fields.AN_Notes: Normatives Rahmenwerk aus Werten, Prinzipien und elf Politikfeldern für Mitgliedstaaten. Bias-Achsen: Geschlecht als eigenes Politikfeld (Policy Area 6, Ziffern 87 bis 93), Sprache und Kultur über die Wirkung von NLP-Anwendungen auf gefährdete Sprachen, Dialekte und tonale Variationen (Policy Area 7, Ziffer 95). Die langen Listen geschützter Merkmale sind Aufzählungen und bleiben uncodiert. Armutslücke (Ziffer 51), Stadt-Land-Gefälle (Ziffern 28, 67) und LMICs behandeln Zugangsungleichheit und digitale Spaltung, nicht Bias eines Systems entlang einer Achse, daher weder Socioeconomic noch Other_Axis. Schadensarten: Stereotypisierung aus dem eigenen Argument zur Reproduktion von Bias und Stereotypen (Ziffern 2(c), 66 und 90), Erasure aus dem Verschwinden gefährdeter Sprachen und Dialekte durch NLP-Anwendungen (Ziffer 95). Diskriminierende algorithmische Entscheidungen (Ziffer 29) werden ohne Zuteilungsfall und ohne Einordnung als unmittelbar oder mittelbar genannt und daher nicht codiert. Maßnahmen: Datenvorbereitung (diverse Trainingsdaten, Gold-Standard-Datensätze, nach Geschlecht disaggregierte Annotation, Ziffern 67 und 76) und Organisation (Ethical Impact Assessment mit Gender-Perspektive, AI Ethics Officers, Aufsicht, Audit, Zertifizierung, diverse Teams), durchgehend als Empfehlung, daher Proposed. AN_Task None: das Instrument regelt die Governance von KI über alle Sektoren und nennt Einsatzfelder wie Gesundheit oder Kulturerbe nur allgemein, ohne eine bestimmte berufliche Aufgabe. Geschlecht erscheint als Mädchen und Frauen gegenüber Männern ohne eigene Bestimmung, strukturelle Gender-Gaps (Ziffer 89) werden benannt, eine ausdrückliche Aussage zu Geschlecht als sozialer Konstruktion fehlt. Bias-Verständnis implizit über Nicht-Diskriminierung im Menschenrechtsrahmen, Ziffer 28 bestimmt Fairness als inklusiven Zugang zu den Vorteilen von KI. Kein Theoriebezug, das Völkerrecht ist ein rechtlich-normativer Bezug. Soziale_Arbeit nein, welfare erscheint nur in einer Aufzählung menschenrechtssensibler Einsatzbereiche (Ziffer 62).
